issues.description: The problem statement contains a contradiction about the type of Animal.name: the UML shows name: String, but the textual instructions explicitly require using StringBuilder for the name attribute. The provided solution implements Animal.name as a String, which conflicts with the textual requirement to use StringBuilder and leaves students unclear which type to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the intended attribute type explicit and consistent across all artifacts. Either update the problem statement so it consistently requires a String (e.g., remove the StringBuilder instruction) or change the solution and any example/template code to use StringBuilder for the Animal.name attribute. If choosing StringBuilder, update Animal.java to declare private StringBuilder name; provide getter/setter signatures consistent with the tests (e.g., getName() returning String or StringBuilder as specified), and update all uses (Seal, Pig, Goat, Farm song messages) to convert to String when needed (for example, getName().toString()).
